home.description: A collection of Aéro's works around the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3) and (4a) Pro. Glyph toys faithfully simulated in the browser, plus the tools that go with them.
home.intro: Index of work around the Glyph Matrix.

lines.sonoglyph: The sound of the mic, measured and drawn with a handful of pixels
lines.justadice: A die with several shapes. Thrown with a shake
lines.gforce: A car accelerometer, inspired by sports cars
lines.float: A bubble level and a compass. Minimal and effective
lines.altclock: An alternative clock, in three typefaces
lines.haloglyph: Future app that will hold the glyph toys, and let you run the glyph matrix as a home screen widget
lines.glyphcast: Turns an image into a Glyph Matrix render

glyphcast.description: Turns an image into a Glyph Matrix render for Nothing Phone (3) and (4a) Pro.
glyphcast.sub: Style an image by projecting it onto the Glyph Matrix

notice.notAnImage: File ignored — an image was expected
notice.frameReloaded: Frame and settings reloaded — drop the image to carry them on

empty.imported: Frame read back from the file. The settings on the right are the ones that produced it — drop the image to carry them on.
empty.none: Matrix off — drop an image anywhere on the page, paste one (Ctrl+V) or use [01] Source.

source.title: Source
source.note: The image is processed locally, in the browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.

mixer.title: Channel mixer
mixer.note: The matrix has no colour: these weights decide how much of each channel goes into the luminance. It is the coloured filter of black and white photography — raising the red lightens skin and darkens a blue sky.

led.title: LED output
led.note: At 2 steps the render goes binary and the dithering does all the work. Past ~16 steps the matrix renders real greys and the dither only serves to break up banding in gradients.

exportCard.title: Export
exportCard.note1: The .json is a drawing in the
exportCard.note2: format — one frame, {leds} LED instructions. It also carries this page's settings, under a key other readers ignore: the same file opens over there and reloads here with all its sliders.

glyphlapse.description: Preview of the GlyphLapse Glyph Toy: time passing, broken down on the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3).
glyphlapse.onlyOne: Only one lapse enabled — the toy has nowhere to switch to

lapse.title: Displayed lapse
lapse.note1: A long press on the Glyph Button moves to the next enabled lapse. Lapse I cannot be disabled: a toy with no active lapse would have nothing to show.
lapse.note2: The selected tab is the one the toy displays: there is no lapse you configure on one side and another that runs on the other. That is how the settings app behaves — picking a tab switches the toy.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.note: A deadline still ahead flips the toy into a countdown. On crossing it, it plays a four-second arrival — the In 5 s button is there to see it without waiting.

format.title: Format
format.note1: Dense writes the whole granularity, two units per line when it has to. Compact keeps only the two leading units, in 5×7. Cycle scrolls them one by one. Days gives the total alone. Hours gives the whole span in hours.
format.compactNote: On Phone (4a) Pro, thirteen columns only fit Cycle — that's the only layout that does.

seconds.title: Seconds
seconds.note1: Ring fills the rim from twelve o'clock — clockwise when time accumulates, anticlockwise when it runs out. Hourglass raises or lowers a level of sand whose surface is a cone: tip at the centre in “since”, funnel in “until”. Diagonal tints the background with an oblique front from the top-left to the bottom-right corner, kept faint so the text stays readable.

readout.title: Readout
readout.note: The breakdown follows the calendar, not a division: two months are 59, 60 or 62 days depending on which. It is the same count as Period.between on the toy side.

glyphslot.description: Preview of the GlyphSlot Glyph Toy: a slot machine on the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3).

status.idle: Long-press the Glyph Button to spin

spinCard.title: Spin
spinCard.note1: The two forcing buttons do not exist on the toy: they are here to see the effects without waiting. A jackpot lands at 5 %, a plain win at 15 % — checking that a seven-second animation reads well by rolling for it is no way to work.
spinCard.note2: On the device the only control is a long press on the Glyph Button. Holding the one in the photo for 450 ms does the same thing.

roll.title: Last spin
roll.note: The payline is the central seven-row window. Neighbouring symbols stay lit at a fifth of the intensity: that is what makes it read as a window onto a spinning band rather than three independent cells.

justadice.description: Preview of the Just a dice Glyph Toy: a die thrown with a shake on the Glyph Matrix of a Nothing Phone.

reject.tooEarly: The die has only just left
reject.tooLate: The die is landing — let it settle
reject.inAir: The die is in the air

status.rest: The die is at rest — shake to throw
status.tumble: It tumbles — a shake throws it again

throwCard.title: Throw
throwCard.forceNote: These buttons do not exist on the toy: they are here to see a given face without waiting for it. The value is drawn at the start anyway — the animation does not discover it, it leads to it.
throwCard.deviceNote: On the device: shaking the phone throws the die — the button above does that. A long press on the Glyph Button changes solid — the selector at the top of the page does that directly.
throwCard.expected: At {throws, plural, one {# throw} other {# throws}}, each face expects {each} — the dotted line.

timing.title: Timing
timing.note1: The red band is the window where a shake throws the die again — before it, the previous gesture is still ending; after it, the die is choosing its face.
timing.note2: Six bounces, then the camera moves in to reveal the top face.

sonoglyph.description: Preview of Sono's three ways to read the sound level — spectrum, needle, waveform — on the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3).
sonoglyph.sub: Visualize the sound from your mic

voice.name: Voice
voice.note: 200 Hz – 4 kHz band, ~4 Hz syllabic modulation

music.name: Music
music.note: 2 Hz pulse, marked bass and short highs

source.title: Source
source.note: Neither computes a level: they produce samples, and it is the toy's chain — A-weighting, Fast detector, band bank — that turns them into a dB. The mic goes through an AudioWorklet, with AGC, noise reduction and echo cancellation switched off. Nothing leaves the browser.

sim.title: Simulated signal
sim.note: The setting is in dB(A) and not dBFS: the gain makes up for what the weighting will take off the chosen timbre, measured when the timbre changes. Without that compensation the slider would lie by 9 dB between the sine and the traffic.

gforce.description: Preview of G-Forces, Haloglyph's car accelerometer: a ball that shows what you're feeling right now, four peaks that show what the drive threw at you.

pad.title: Acceleration
pad.label: Simulated push
pad.note1: The pad simulates the push a corner or a braking would give you — toward the top is braking. On the device it is the phone's accelerometer, projected onto the horizontal plane to cancel out the mount's tilt.

peaks.title: Drive peaks
peaks.note1: Peaks are not kept: on the device as here, closing the toy clears them — a peak is the story of a drive, not a record.

float.description: Preview of Float, Haloglyph's bubble level and compass: a logarithmic scale that makes a tenth of a degree visible, and a four-letter rose.

instrument.title: Displayed instrument
instrument.heading: Simulated heading
instrument.note1: The pad simulates the phone's pose: flat at the centre, standing on edge at the rim — which is what flips the level from the flat regime to the plumb one, as on the device.

altclock.description: Preview of Alt Clock, an alternative clock for the Glyph Matrix: the time in big digits, in three typefaces.
altclock.note1: A clock designed to be customised. Vertical layout on the Phone (3), to match the stock clock of the (4a) Pro.

haloglyph.description: Haloglyph: the pack that bundles this repo's Glyph toys into one Android app for the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3), and into a widget that emulates it elsewhere.
haloglyph.sub: The pack that bundles the toys

pitch.note1: HALOGLYPH bundles this repo's Glyph toys into a single Android app: on the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3) through Glyph Interface, and — lacking a matrix — into a home-screen widget that emulates it pixel for pixel on any other phone.
pitch.note2: Still a draft: the six toys are written, registered with the system, and already running in the widget, but the pack isn't published. Glyphslot isn't part of it — a slot machine forces a rating that would contaminate the rest of the pack — and stays a repo of its own.

toys.title: The toys
toys.note1: Each one switches on a long press of the Glyph Button — or a tap, in the widget.
toys.glyphlapse: A time counter: up to five deadlines, as a ring or an hourglass.
toys.justadice: d6, d10, d12, d20 tracked in quaternions — shake to throw.
toys.sonoglyph: The mic on the matrix, as spectrum, needle, or wave.
toys.float: A bubble level on a logarithmic scale, and a compass as second instrument.
toys.gforce: A car accelerometer: a ball for right now, four peaks for the drive.
toys.altclock: An alternative clock: the time in big digits, in three typefaces.

widget.title: The widget
widget.note1: One widget carries every toy: tap to interact with whichever is shown, double tap to move to the next, long press to change what it shows. Two sizes, 2 × 2 and 1 × 1 — up to three widgets placed at once.
widget.note2: A burst lasts thirty seconds; a widget can also run continuously, and suspends itself as soon as the screen turns off.

build.title: Build
build.note1: Five languages — de, en, es, fr, it, English as fallback — the same set as the rest of the ecosystem: translation reaches down to the unit shown on the matrix.
build.note2: JDK 17, Android SDK 36, no Nothing API key required. The GlyphMatrixSDK downloads itself on the first build.
